your_book:
Thursday was a tale of two tapes for Jaleel's book. The standout mover was RKLB, which surged +10.38% on the session — the largest day-gain in the portfolio — yet remains deep in the red at –17.5% overall and carries an AVOID verdict with a QARP score of just 46. That divergence is worth sitting with: a single-day pop doesn't rehabilitate a thesis that was never strongly held, and at 14.3% of the book it is the single largest position. On the positive side, AVGO (+4.73%) and NVDA (+2.65%) caught a tailwind from Microsoft AI-infrastructure optimism, adding modest support. NBIX also ticked up +2.61% and is now +13.8% on cost — one of the cleaner wins in the book.

The drag came from the software cluster and medical devices. ADBE fell –5.9% and NOW dropped –4.92% — both despite a sector headline suggesting software was actually rallying into Microsoft's earnings. That's a red flag: if the tide was coming in and these names still sold off, something idiosyncratic is weighing on them. EFX dropped –5.84% with no clear catalyst provided. ABT (–2.21%) and ZTS (–2.44%) gave back ground despite both carrying STRONG BUY verdicts and solid QARP scores — likely noise, but worth monitoring given ABT's existing EPS-guide flag. The portfolio's overall unrealized gain sits at just +$143.68 (+0.64%), reflecting how much dead weight RKLB's –17.5% hole and several other underwater names represent against the winners.

The drift that deserves scrutiny: BSX sits at –3.9% overall with a guidance-slashed flag (FY26 growth cut to 7–8.5%, flat through Q3 guided), yet it barely moved today (–0.09%) and still holds a STRONG BUY verdict with an 80.4 QARP. Price and analyst verdict are pulling against the fundamental risk flag — that tension needs resolution before the next earnings in October. Similarly, LULU is –6.6% overall with a guidance-cut flag and five straight quarters of negative Americas comps, yet it edged up +0.37% today. The next read is September 2 — that's the moment of truth.

attention.headline: Largest position, AVOID-rated, –17.5% in the hole — today's 10% pop changes nothing structurally
attention.note: At 14.3% of the book, RKLB is both the biggest weight and the lowest-conviction name (QARP 46, AVOID verdict); the day's gain looks like noise given no fundamental catalyst was cited — Jaleel needs to decide whether to use this strength to reduce or exit rather than let a bounce mask a broken thesis.

attention.headline: Fell –5.9% on a day the software sector was broadly rallying — divergence is a warning sign
attention.note: The headline context was positive for software yet ADBE underperformed badly, which reinforces the existing AI-disruption narrative risk and CFO-exit overhang; if it can't participate in a sector up-day, the next catalyst (Sep 10 earnings) carries asymmetric downside.

attention.headline: –4.92% despite a software rally day; highest dollar weight in the book
attention.note: NOW is the largest-weight high-multiple name and it sold off on a day its sector was cited as a beneficiary — that relative weakness, combined with its known macro-beta risk flag, warrants watching closely ahead of its October 27 earnings.

attention.headline: STRONG BUY verdict sits uneasily against a slashed guidance flag and –3.9% unrealized loss
attention.note: Management guided flat through Q3 and cut FY26 growth to 7–8.5%, yet the system still rates it STRONG BUY (QARP 80.4) — Jaleel should verify whether that verdict has been updated to reflect the guidance cut, or whether there's a stale-rating risk heading into the October 20 print.
